Housing & Affordability: slot: FHFA house price index by MSA
Safety & Quality of Life: slot: EPA air quality by metro
Overall Tech-Hub Comparisons: slot: CBRE or Brookings tech-talent report
Community Perspectives: slot: local subreddit AMA or city-forum thread

sources.title: Metropolitan Occupational Employment and Wage Estimates
sources.covers: Employment counts and wage estimates for occupations across U.S. metro areas, including computer and technology occupations.
sources.value: Government data rather than a private ranking, so job-market strength and pay can be compared metro to metro on a consistent method.
sources.aud: Someone comparing cities for a tech career.
sources.lim: Covers jobs and wages only — says nothing about housing, safety, or quality of life.

sources.title: 2024 American Community Survey — Selected Housing Characteristics (DP04)
sources.covers: Rent, home values, total housing costs, vacancy, and share of income going toward housing.
sources.value: Housing drives whether a salary actually goes far; ACS gives a reliable metro-level comparison instead of state averages.
sources.aud: Anyone comparing housing costs between cities.
sources.lim: Large tables to sort through, and it never puts housing cost next to local tech salaries.

sources.title: Comprehensive Housing Market Analysis — North Port–Sarasota–Bradenton, FL
sources.pub: U.S. Dept. of Housing and Urban Development
sources.covers: One metro in depth: employment, population growth, home sales, rentals, construction, and forecast housing demand.
sources.value: A close read of a market I would actually consider, which can be set against salary and job data from the other sources.
sources.aud: Someone considering the Sarasota area for work or relocation.
sources.lim: Sarasota is a smaller tech market than Austin or Raleigh, so it does not generalize.

sources.path: Cost of Living › Metro Price Levels
sources.title: Regional Price Parities by State and Metro Area
sources.covers: Price levels compared between states and metro areas as an index against the national average.
sources.value: Turns raw salary into purchasing power — the single most useful adjustment in the whole collection.
sources.aud: Anyone comparing affordability or purchasing power between cities.
sources.lim: An overall price measure; it will not match any individual's real spending mix.

sources.path: Safety & Quality of Life › Crime & Safety
sources.title: 2024 Reported Crimes in the Nation
sources.covers: Violent and property crime reported by law-enforcement agencies across the country.
sources.value: A defensible safety source in place of an online “safest cities” ranking with an unclear method.
sources.aud: Anyone comparing places to live who wants safety in the decision.
sources.lim: Metro-level totals hide big differences between neighborhoods, and reporting coverage varies by agency.

sources.title: Best Cities for Tech Jobs in 2026 — Salary and Demand Data
sources.covers: Major U.S. metros ranked on tech job demand, salaries, hiring growth, and cost-of-living-adjusted pay.
sources.value: Combines several parts of the topic at once, which is a useful cross-check on my own metro comparisons.
sources.aud: Students, recent grads, or anyone comparing cities for a tech career.
sources.lim: Built from InsideTrack's own job-listing database, so it under-represents employers who post elsewhere.

sources.path: Community Perspectives › Living in Tech Cities
sources.title: r/SameGrassButGreener — “B-list” tech cities that are actually nice places to live?
sources.covers: A discussion of smaller or less obvious tech cities that may still have strong jobs and be enjoyable to live in.
sources.value: Residents raise things a government report never shows — the reason the collection has a qualitative category at all.
sources.aud: Someone trying to get a more personal feel for different cities.
sources.lim: Opinion based; comments are never used as proof of a factual claim.
